steps.body: Metaphor (direct comparison), simile (like/as), personification (human qualities to non-human)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Imagery: visual, auditory, tactile, olfactory, gustatory; extended metaphors

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Sound devices: alliteration, assonance, consonance, onomatopoeia, sibilance

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Structure: stanza types, rhyme (ABAB, AABB, free verse), metre (iambic, trochaic), line breaks

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Q: Analyse how the poet uses structure and language to convey the theme of loss in 'When You Are Old' by Yeats --- Solution: Three stanzas move from present to past to future. Iambic pentameter creates reflective tone. 'Glad grace' (alliteration) contrasts with 'pilgrim soul' (metaphor). Final stanza 'bending down beside the glowing bars' -- imagery of ageing/regret. ABBA rhyme encloses memory
